title: Most Frogs Pull Their Eyeballs Into Their Mouths When They Swallow
hook: When the northern leopard frog swallows prey, it shuts its eyes and pulls them down into its mouth

open.title: Frogs shut their eyes when they swallow, and those eyes have another job
open.line: A frog shuts its eyes again and again while it swallows something. But they do more than close. Where do the eyes go?

summary: Most frogs close their eyes when they swallow and pull them down into the mouth. The eyes seem to help push the food toward the throat.

text: Most frogs close their eyes again and again while swallowing food.
In 2004, a research team filmed northern leopard frogs swallowing prey with X-ray video.
It turned out the eyes don't just close.
The eyeballs and eye muscles seemed to sink deep into the mouth and touch the food.
The team concluded that the eyes help push the food toward the throat.
Even when the nerves to the muscles that pull both eyes in were cut, the frog could still swallow prey.

panels.text: So the eyes aren't needed, right?

text: Instead, the swallows needed to get one prey down rose from 2.3 on average to 4.
